entries.clue: Point to that woman's father, a mountain guide (6)

blocks.note: S = south, a point of the compass

annotation.surface: Someone directs you to a woman's dad, who leads climbs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like a verb, to point someone towards; it is a noun, one of the compass points.
annotation.definitionFit: Sherpas, a Himalayan people, are famed as guides and porters on mountain expeditions.

entries.clue: Promote right industry with excessive energy (13)

annotation.surface: A call to boost the right-wing business sector, which has too much drive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Industry' reads as manufacturing; here it means diligence, being busy.
annotation.definitionFit: Hyperactivity is abnormally high energy and restlessness.

annotation.surface: A cook points to the underdone portion of a dish that tastes good.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Savoury' looks like an adjective describing the part; it is a noun, in the British sense of a small salty dish served at the end of a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit, cheese sauce on toast, is a classic British savoury.

entries.clue: Traffic jam announced by newsreader's assistant (7)

indicatorNotes.announced: an announcement is spoken, so the sound of the words counts

blocks.note: a traffic jam is a queue of autos (cars)

annotation.surface: A traffic jam is reported on the news.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a travel bulletin; the newsreader is really reading from the device, not reporting the jam.
annotation.definitionFit: An Autocue is the screen that scrolls the script in front of a newsreader's camera.

indicatorNotes.admitting: to admit is to let in, so SHY takes ODD inside it

annotation.surface: A description of a shy, strange person without money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poor' reads as short of money; it means badly made.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: poor in the sense of badly made, as with cheap goods or careless workmanship.

blocks.note: a pointed pole driven into the ground, e.g. to hold up a fence
the sum a gambler puts down on an outcome

annotation.surface: Place a wager, perhaps online.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Post' reads as a verb, to post a bet; it is a noun, a pole in the ground, and STAKE is also the wager itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Stake means both a pointed post and the sum put on a bet.

indicatorNotes.to play: the letters are set to play, moving about freely

annotation.surface: Eight musicians and others about to perform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play' sits naturally beside 'players', so it reads as music rather than as an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Oct- is the Latin root for eight, as in octopus, and in music the word names a group of eight performers or a piece for them.

entries.clue: Anything caught by dodgy new laird is relative (8-2-3)

indicatorNotes.caught by: AUGHT is caught, held inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.dodgy: dodgy = unreliable, so NEW LAIRD is rearranged

blocks.note: anagram of NEW LAIRD, split D…ERINLAW around AUGHT

annotation.surface: Whatever a shady new Scottish landowner catches turns out to be family.
annotation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner. AUGHT, an archaic word for anything, goes after the D of the rearranged letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a son's wife joins the family by marriage, the 'in-law' kind of relative.

indicatorNotes.spoiling: spoilt letters are damaged out of their order

annotation.surface: A tape snapped and ruined a recording of some music.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a broken cassette spoiling a piece of music, so 'musical work' reads as the victim rather than the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short, light opera.

indicatorNotes.soundly: by sound: the answer is heard, not spelt

annotation.surface: Someone is nervous, though well trained.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly', qualifying 'instructed'; it signals a word heard aloud.
annotation.definitionFit: Taut means stretched tight, tense.

entries.clue: Crustacean initially crawls round alabaster bust (4)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the initial, first, letter of each following word

annotation.surface: A crab scuttles around a white stone sculpture.
annotation.walkthrough: The four words after 'initially' supply one letter each; the surface image of a crab on a bust keeps you reading them as a scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the crab is the best-known crustacean, the hard-shelled class that also takes in lobsters and shrimps.

indicatorNotes.sound like: says outright that the answer is heard as another word

annotation.surface: Quick operators are rumoured to be swindlers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast movers' reads as smooth operators, people, which fits the tricksters; they are animals.
annotation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

blocks.note: the surface reading: coughs and wheezes, a bad chest
the setter's reading: what the Grim Reaper wields, and a fatal chest illness is what brings his blade

annotation.surface: A harvester with a bad cough.
annotation.walkthrough: The reaper is the Grim Reaper, Death, who carries a scythe; fatal chest illness is what brings his blade to you.
annotation.definitionFit: A scythe is the long curved blade the Grim Reaper carries.

indicatorNotes.spread around: AS is spread so that its letters sit around GATE

annotation.surface: Jewels scattered about a doorway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a filler word in the surface; it is the outer pair of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Agates are banded semi-precious stones.

blocks.note: an ant is an insect, a bug

annotation.surface: Treatment for an insect sting.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a sting cream; the remedy is for heartburn, and ants do sting with acid.
annotation.definitionFit: An antacid is a medicine that neutralises stomach acid.

entries.clue: Limited in arsenic, yet is plentiful (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one word inside another: the word for limited sits inside the symbol for arsenic

blocks.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic, split A…S

annotation.surface: Arsenic is only allowed in small quantities, yet there's lots of it about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Limited' reads as describing the arsenic; it is the word that goes inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with the verb kept: to exist in great numbers, and 'is plentiful' is a verb phrase too.

entries.clue: See sports event in fabric dressing, having strained this tissue? (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one word inside another: the sports event sits inside the fabric dressing

blocks.note: lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds, split LI…NT

annotation.surface: Watch a match with your leg bandaged after an injury.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition leans on the surface: a strained ligament is exactly why you would be watching sport in a dressing.
annotation.definitionFit: A ligament is the tough tissue joining bone to bone, often strained in sport.

annotation.surface: Every evening I'm home and exhausted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All in' is British slang for exhausted.
annotation.definitionFit: All-in means completely worn out, dog-tired.

indicatorNotes.inside: the answer is found inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'when' into the start of 'rolling'

annotation.surface: Register while you're on a roll, or while the money's rolling in.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap: the EN of 'when' plus the ROL of 'rolling'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you sign up for a course, a club or the army.

blocks.note: OM = Order of Merit, a British honour

annotation.surface: Skip it, even though you were told to do it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a command; it is the Order of Merit, a British honour abbreviated OM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to skip something from a list or text, deliberately or by oversight.

blocks.note: a statement of money owed, as handed over in a restaurant
the programme of what is showing, as in 'top of the ...'

annotation.surface: Paying for the cinema's programme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Account for' reads as a phrasal verb, explain; 'for' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Bill means both an invoice and a programme of entertainment.

entries.clue: Small amount of money in trust not so long ago (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one word inside another: the small coin goes inside the verb for trust

blocks.note: to rely = to trust, split RE…LY
a cent is a small coin

annotation.surface: A little money was put into a trust fund not long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trust' reads as a trust fund, a noun; it is the verb rely.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adverb places something at a time just past.

blocks.note: the surface reading is loudness; the setter means a book
hymns are songs of praise, so this is a book of them

annotation.surface: How loudly someone is applauded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Volume' reads as loudness; it is a book.
annotation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a book of hymns, songs of praise.

indicatorNotes.amid: 'amid' means in the middle of, so the pig stands in the middle of the noise

blocks.note: a din is a loud noise, split DI…N
a sow is a female pig

annotation.surface: Leaving a pig behind in the racket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pig' is the specific female, the sow, a crossword favourite.
annotation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to abandon them, refusing any connection.
